note: Skill health (failures, degraded state) is derived on demand from decisions.jsonl by HEAL_CIRCUIT_STATUS, not tracked as live state here — an agent cannot reliably keep persistent counters up to date across sessions. 'version' here is this file's own schema/catalog-format version (bump on structural changes to how skills are described), not the framework's ai_os_version in manifest.json — commands/index.json's 'version' field is the same kind of catalog-schema version, tracked independently per file since the two catalogs' shapes can and do change on different schedules. 'pointer_description' (optional, EP-88) is the always-loaded text for host-native skill pointers (INSTALL_PROMPT.md Step 3): it leads with the situations that should load the skill, kept short because every session pays for it; absent -> 'description' is used.

skills.name: Security Audit & Enforcement
skills.description: Vulnerability scanning, dependency auditing, pre-commit security gates, and emergency lockdown.
skills.pointer_description: Use before writing or changing code that touches auth, input handling, secrets, shell/SQL/eval, or dependencies; when asked for a security audit or scan; or when a breach or leaked credential is suspected.

skills.name: Infrastructure & Scaffolding
skills.description: Tech stack detection, project scaffolding, CI/CD generation, and health diagnostics.
skills.pointer_description: Use when detecting or changing the tech stack, scaffolding a project or CI, the build or environment is broken, mapping modules or data flow, analyzing commit history, or isolating a branch in a git worktree.

skills.name: Testing & Validation
skills.description: Test execution, coverage analysis, AI-assisted test generation, and impact analysis.
skills.pointer_description: Use when writing code test-first, running or generating tests, checking coverage, deciding which tests a change affects, or guarding a fixed bug with a regression test.

skills.name: Self-Evolution Engine
skills.description: PDCA-based self-improvement lifecycle - propose, apply, verify, and rollback system evolutions.
skills.pointer_description: Use when improving the AI OS framework itself: proposing, applying, rolling back, or reviewing changes to its skills, commands, rules, or workflows.

skills.name: Observability & Audit Trail
skills.description: Decision logging, action tracing, session export, and health reporting.
skills.pointer_description: Use when logging a significant decision or action, tracing what happened in a session, or reporting progress or framework health.

skills.name: Context Engineering Engine
skills.description: Guidance for intelligent context assembly, relevance scoring, and pruning what you actively choose to read.
skills.pointer_description: Use when a task needs more files than fit comfortably, when deciding what to read for a multi-part task, or when context is getting crowded and needs pruning.

skills.name: Memory Lifecycle
skills.description: Backs TASK_CLOSE and MEMORY_CONSOLIDATE: verify-before-promote, diff-before-delete, dedup, collision-safe task-file resolution, orphan sweep, and archive pruning for the task -> archived -> semantic pipeline.
skills.pointer_description: Use when closing a task or branch, consolidating or pruning memory, or when a project-knowledge entry is wrong, stale, or contradicts the code.
skills.note: commands lists this skill's own skill_commands; backs_builtin_commands lists built-ins (see commands/index.json's system_commands) whose procedure this skill defines but doesn't own the entry for — kept separate so registry/commands consistency checks don't flag them as drift.

skills.name: Self-Healing & Resilience
skills.description: Loop detection, failure classification, auto-repair, and emergency protocols.
skills.pointer_description: Use when a test or build fails, an error repeats or a fix didn't stick, a bug needs its root cause before a fix, framework files look broken, or a claim needs a credibility check before reporting.

skills.name: Architect - Idea to Project
skills.description: Transforms a raw idea into a fully planned and scaffolded project through structured interview, architecture design, and automated scaffolding.
skills.pointer_description: Use when the user wants to start a new project from an idea: interview, architecture design, and scaffolding from an empty or near-empty workspace.

skills.name: Planning - Brainstorm, Write, Execute
skills.description: Per-feature brainstorm -> write-plan -> execute cycle for work inside an existing project, distinct from architect.sk's greenfield-only scope.
skills.pointer_description: Use when a feature or change inside an existing project needs clarifying, a written step-by-step plan, plan execution, or a retrospective.

skills.name: Simplicity - Complexity Governance
skills.description: Pre-mutation simplicity ladder, deliberate-shortcut marker convention (AIOS-DEBT:), and over-engineering-scoped review/audit passes. Covers the gap R22 leaves: R22 forbids bundling unrequested refactors, nothing gates the requested work itself on necessity.
skills.pointer_description: Use before writing new code to check whether less code, the stdlib, or the platform already solves it; when reviewing a diff or codebase for over-engineering; or when taking a deliberate shortcut.

skills.name: Dev Loop - Implementation with Peer Review
skills.description: Implementation with independent peer review when the host supports subagent dispatch; honestly-labeled same-agent fallback when it doesn't.
skills.pointer_description: Use when implementing a feature or fix that should get an independent review, especially small work without a plan.
